title: NFR-007 takeover: the human mutex blocks the agent in every workflow state
risk: Takeover works in the chat screen but a background campaign or a cart-recovery workflow keeps messaging the same customer, so the human's answer is contradicted by the platform.
preconditions: Namespace gov-nfr-<case_id>-<worker_id>; NFR verification runs against the offline gateway with mock SoR and channel boundaries.
Frozen clock 2026-01-15T10:00:00Z; failure, outage and crash injections are scripted at the substituted boundary, never faked inside the assertion.
Conversation conv-nfr-7 has a cart-recovery reminder scheduled to fire after the takeover.

steps.action: Acquire the takeover lease for the customer conversation
steps.expected: Status becomes HUMAN_TAKEOVER and the mutex key exists for the conversation.

steps.action: Let the scheduled background reminder fire
steps.expected: The reminder is blocked by the mutex with a 409 and no message is delivered to the customer.

steps.action: Send an operator reply and then resume
steps.expected: The operator reply is delivered once; after resume the next agent action is permitted again.

assertions: The mutex suppresses every agent-originated send for the conversation, including background workflows - not just interactive replies.
Adapter counter shows one operator message and zero agent messages during the takeover.
Resume restores agent messaging without sending an accumulated backlog of blocked reminders.
The blocked reminder is recorded with the mutex reason rather than being silently dropped.
forbidden: Applying the takeover only to the interactive reply path.
Delivering the blocked reminders in a burst immediately after resume.
Treating resume as a new authority grant.
evidence: Mutex key lifecycle and conversation status history.
Adapter message log with sender attribution and counts.
Blocked reminder records with the 409 reason.
cleanup: Resume if needed and delete gov- conversation and reminder rows.
automation: Core PEP, rules engine, audit writer, idempotency store and worker lease logic run as real code under test; only ERP/WMS, channel gateways, Redis and the model provider are substituted. Faults are injected at those boundaries and waits are condition-based on persisted state.
